findings.subject: src/wave1/func_0018fd20.cpp:9-13 and src/wave1/func_0018fdd4.cpp:12-15
findings.summary: Share one identical Result definition across the C++ units. Both new translation units define the same namespace-scope class Result, and both use that class as their exported function result, but only func_0018fd20.cpp includes failed(). These are not translation-unit-local types: the combined ledger therefore contains different definitions of one external-linkage C++ class and violates the one-definition rule. Separate MATCH runs cannot detect this ill-formed combined C++ program, and both units were skipped by the mechanical interface checker. Put the complete identical definition in a shared header used by both units (or give genuinely distinct helper types distinct identities) before accepting their waived interfaces.
findings.title: Share one identical Result definition across the C++ units

findings.subject: src/wave1/func_00196cb8.c:31 and checkpoint c002-wave1 known-issues disclosure
findings.summary: Publish the new checkpoint qualifications before acceptance. This new function explicitly preserves the invalid-screen indexing path, and c002 also adds nine mechanically unchecked C++ units with partial declarations, but the only published known-issues documents cover c001 and its 17-function scope. There is no docs/known-issues-c002-wave1.md or other known-issues entry covering these new functions. D8 in docs/ACCEPTANCE.md requires checkpoint-specific publication of preserved original bugs, skips and qualifications; record the conditional invalid-screen behavior, unrecovered bounds and new C++ waiver/type limitations there. The source ORIGINAL BUG comment is present and the current bytes MATCH; this is a disclosure omission, not a newly introduced runtime indexing change.
findings.title: Publish the new checkpoint preserved-behavior qualifications

qualifications: All 38 new functions were independently rerun sequentially with tools/match.py and profile game: 38 MATCH results covering 1584 new bytes. Read both prepared fresh full-build receipts: each records 55 total credited functions and 2680 bytes including the accepted c001 baseline, equal code.bin/ExeFS .code hashes and no cached unit. No full build or test suite was rerun by this reviewer.

Catalogue v3 was checked directly for all 38 addresses: every credited owner is kind function, none is a veneer or multi_entry. The forwarded callee entry 0x12d5c4 was inspected inside its non-credited multi_entry owner 0x12d5c0; it is not credited by this checkpoint.

All nine new C++ units were manually interface-checked against current C/C++ units and independently regenerated original packets; F01 is the outstanding cross-unit source defect. Apart from that defect, the exercised parameter, return and virtual-dispatch ABI agrees with the target. Resource classes, tagged handles, destructor reconstruction and other padded structs are partial 32-bit target descriptions, not fully recovered types or portable native-port proofs.

The shared CommandSystem header was read and its +0x11/+0x12, +0x9c/+0xa0, +0x158 and +0x160 fields were checked against both users and original queue/counter accesses. The produced command kind 1 has an explicit consuming dispatcher branch forwarding its source and size; no silent-drop integration defect was found there.

func_00196cb8 retains the original invalid-screen before-table path if the error handler returns, with an ORIGINAL BUG comment; valid-screen/index preconditions and error-handler return behavior are not established here. This is preserved target behavior rather than a proposed fix. Its checkpoint-specific disclosure is F02.

Inherited in-place hybrid-build limitations remain: a complete original-armlink reconstruction, unwind coverage, cross-host reproduction and lower RomFS IVFC traversal are separate unproven properties. Exact current target matching does not certify them.
